chunks: Saad from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masru Masruq, from al-Sindi ibn Muhammad, from Yahya ibn Amr al-Zayyat, from Dawud ibn Kathir al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'All people live in the surplus of our oppression, except that we have exempted our Shias from that.'

key_terms.فَضْلِ: Surplus, excess, or benefit derived from something.
key_terms.مَظْلِمَتِنَا: Our oppression (referring to the Ahl al-Bayt).

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that people live in the surplus of the Imams' oppression?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) articulates a profound theological concept where the suffering of the Ahl al-Bayt generates a spiritual surplus (*fadl*) that benefits all of humanity, effectively turning their oppression into a source of universal merit. However, the Shia are uniquely exempted from this general benefit, implying that their close association with the Imams requires them to bear the cost of this spiritual capital directly or that they are protected from the 'debt' of the Imams' suffering, highlighting their distinct, elevated status in the cosmic order.
